row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 1, which of the following best describes the radiographic features that support the diagnosis of bronchial atresia in this patient?

A) A round opacity in the right upper lung zone with surrounding normal lung parenchyma and abundant vasculature.
B) A tubular or nodular opacity extending from the hilum in the right upper lung zone surrounded by hyperlucent lung parenchyma with decreased vascular markings.
C) A small solitary nodule in the right upper lung zone with surrounding dense lung parenchyma and increased vascular markings.
D) A large mass in the right upper lung zone with multiple calcifications and surrounding hyperlucent lung parenchyma.
E) A diffuse opacity in both upper lung zones with normal vascular markings and no areas of hyperlucency.
F) A linear opacity in the right lower lung zone with surrounding normal lung parenchyma and increased vascular markings.

reference.correct_choice_text: A tubular or nodular opacity extending from the hilum in the right upper lung zone surrounded by hyperlucent lung parenchyma with decreased vascular markings.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When CXR shows unilateral lung hyperlucency with reduced vascular markings and small hilum, but side assignment is ambiguous due to rotation or mediastinal shift
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect rib spacing and diaphragm position: reduced intercostal space + elevated hemidiaphragm on the same side confirms volume loss (not hyperinflation); correlate with hilum size and vascular tapering
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable in severe scoliosis or if diaphragm obscured by gastric air; requires adequate inspiration

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When initial CXR shows lower lung opacity with diaphragmatic silhouetting and lateral confirmation of posterior basal location, and follow-up shows volume loss plus new apical lucency
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for visceral pleural line at apex on PA view and check lateral for absence of lung markings beyond anterior chest wall; confirm no mediastinal shift
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: May miss small pneumothorax if overpenetrated or obscured by surgical hardware; requires comparison with prior films
